rules.title: String literal escape set
rules.statement: String literals support the escape sequences \\, \", \n, \r, \t, \0, and \xHH (two hex digits) for control bytes < 0x20; all other bytes appear verbatim.

rules.title: Binary operator is infix
rules.statement: A binary operation is written `lhs OP rhs` with OP an infix operator token.

rules.title: Unary operators are prefix
rules.statement: Unary operators (`&`, `!`, `-`, etc.) are prefix and bind directly to their operand with no intervening space: `OP operand`.

rules.title: Cast syntax
rules.statement: A cast is written `expr as Type`.

rules.title: Dereference operator
rules.statement: Dereference is written with prefix `*`: `*expr`.

rules.title: Free-function turbofish placement
rules.statement: Explicit type arguments to a free-function call use turbofish after the callee name and before the argument list: `callee::<T1, T2>(args)`.

rules.title: Static-call turbofish precedes method name
rules.statement: In an associated/static call, turbofish type arguments attach to the receiver type and precede the `::method` segment: `Recv::<T>::method(args)`.
rules.divergence: Rust places the turbofish after the method for trait/inherent fns (e.g. T::method::<U>); Logos surface form puts it before the method name on the type path.

rules.title: Method-call turbofish placement
rules.statement: A method call is `receiver.method(args)`; explicit type arguments are turbofish placed after the method name: `receiver.method::<T>(args)`.

rules.title: Field access
rules.statement: Named field access is `receiver.field`.

rules.title: Tuple index access
rules.statement: Tuple element access uses a numeric field after a dot: `receiver.N`.

rules.title: Index expression
rules.statement: Indexing is written `receiver[index]`.

rules.title: One-element tuple requires trailing comma
rules.statement: A tuple literal is `(e0, e1, ...)`; a single-element tuple is distinguished from a parenthesized expression by a mandatory trailing comma: `(e,)`.

rules.title: Array literal
rules.statement: An array literal is a comma-separated element list in brackets: `[e0, e1, ...]`.

rules.title: Struct literal field forms
rules.statement: A struct literal is `Name { f: v, ... }`; fields are either `name: value` (FIELD_INIT) or shorthand `name` (FIELD_SHORTHAND). The name may carry turbofish type args `Name::<T> { ... }`.

rules.title: if and if-let
rules.statement: `if cond { ... }` takes a boolean condition; `if let PAT = expr { ... }` matches a pattern. An `else` branch is either a block or a chained `else if`.

rules.title: match arm syntax
rules.statement: `match scrutinee { PAT [if GUARD] => RHS, ... }`; each arm has an optional `if`-guard and an arm body that is either a block or an expression followed by a comma.

rules.title: Writ literal outer `@` prefix
rules.statement: Writ (data) literals in expression position are introduced with a leading `@`: `@null`, `@true`/`@false`, `@INT`, `@-INT`, `@FLOAT`, `@"str"`, `@{ ... }` (map), `@[ ... ]` (array).
rules.divergence: Logos-specific Writ data-literal syntax; no Rust equivalent.

rules.title: Writ map entry syntax
rules.statement: A Writ map literal `@{ ... }` contains comma-separated entries `key: value`; nested scalar values omit the `@` prefix in inner position.

rules.title: Embedded type in Writ literal
rules.statement: A Logos type can be embedded inside a Writ literal as `<type:T>`.

rules.title: WritStatic const-generic slot type
rules.statement: A slot of a WritStatic-typed const-generic is referenced as `<type:CFG.slot.path>` with dot-separated step names.

rules.title: Writ antiquotation capture syntax
rules.statement: Within a quoted/Writ literal, an antiquotation captures a value either by identifier `$name` or by expression block `${expr}`.
rules.divergence: Logos metaprogramming antiquotation; no Rust equivalent.

rules.title: Antiquoted callee drops synthetic first arg
rules.statement: When a call's callee is produced by antiquotation substitution, the grammar's bulk `$...` capture inserts the antiquot payload as the first argument; semantically that first argument is not a real call argument and is skipped.
rules.uncertainty: Inferred from renderer mirroring lower_call; exact substitution mechanism defined elsewhere.

rules.title: unsafe block as expression
rules.statement: An `unsafe { ... }` block may appear in expression position (e.g. as a let initializer).

rules.title: Binding and wildcard patterns
rules.statement: A wildcard pattern is `_`; a named binding pattern is the identifier itself.

rules.title: Literal patterns
rules.statement: Patterns may be integer literals (optionally negated with leading `-`), boolean literals (`true`/`false`), or unit `()`.

rules.title: Variant pattern forms
rules.statement: An enum variant pattern is written `Enum::Variant` (data-less) or with data `Enum::Variant(args)`; the bare/tuple-struct form `Variant(args)` omits the enum qualifier.

rules.title: Tuple pattern trailing comma
rules.statement: A tuple pattern is `(p0, p1, ...)`; a single-element tuple pattern requires a trailing comma `(p,)`.

rules.title: Or-pattern
rules.statement: Alternative patterns are combined with `|`: `p0 | p1 | ...`.

rules.title: Range pattern is inclusive
rules.statement: A range pattern is written `lo..=hi` (inclusive); either bound may be negated with a leading `-`.
rules.uncertainty: Renderer only emits `..=`; exclusive range patterns (if any) not represented here.

rules.title: Reference pattern
rules.statement: A reference pattern is `&pat` or `&mut pat`.

rules.title: Rest pattern
rules.statement: A rest/ignore-remaining pattern is written `..` and may appear among struct or tuple subpatterns.

rules.title: Struct pattern
rules.statement: A struct pattern is `Name { field [: subpat], ..., [..] }`; a field with no `: subpat` binds by field name (shorthand), and a trailing `..` ignores remaining fields.
